usdRate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, exchange rates (USD middle rate, noon)
usdRate.note: 4.0635 ringgit per US dollar on 30 Oct 2026 as read by the researcher; when re-checked on 3 Nov the same BNM page showed 4.0665 (2 Nov) and 4.0750 (3 Nov), consistent with this level.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Department of Statistics Malaysia CPI (via Trading Economics)
inflation_cpi.note: 1.8% year on year in September 2026, down from 1.9% in August; core 1.7%. DOSM release page returned an error, so a secondary source is used.

inflation_projection.sourceName: 5-year CPI average (2021-2025 about 2.3%); Bank Negara Malaysia has no numeric target
inflation_projection.note: CPI averaged about 2.3% over 2021-2025 and BNM expects prices to stay elevated on energy costs, so we plan with a rounded 2.5%.

policy_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia Monetary Policy Statement, 3 September 2026

savings_account_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, Monthly Highlights & Statistics September 2026, Table 2.1 Interest Rates: Banking Institutions (commercial banks)
savings_account_rate.note: Average savings deposit rate of commercial banks 0.64% in September 2026 (weighted average 0.32%).

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, Monthly Highlights & Statistics September 2026, Table 2.1 Interest Rates: Banking Institutions (commercial banks)
fdr_3m_rate.note: Average 3-month fixed deposit rate of commercial banks 2.15% in September 2026 (weighted average 1.80%); promotional rates can be higher.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, Monthly Highlights & Statistics September 2026, Table 2.1 Interest Rates: Banking Institutions (commercial banks)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Average 12-month fixed deposit rate of commercial banks 2.19% in September 2026 (weighted average 1.92%).

dps_rate.note: No common monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate found; Malaysians save monthly through fixed deposits, unit trusts or EPF voluntary contributions.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: World Bank WDI, deposit interest rate (FR.INR.DPST)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: 2.42% average for 2025 (World Bank). BNM Table 2.1 shows the weighted average 12-month fixed deposit rate at 1.92% in September 2026.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: Malaysia has no standing government savings certificate for individuals; the last retail government sukuk (Sukuk Prihatin) was a one-off 2020 issue.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, government securities yield (Malaysian Treasury Bills, up to 3 months)
tbill_91d_rate.note: Up to 3-month Malaysian Treasury Bill yield 2.98% on the BNM page; still 2.98% when re-checked on 2 Nov 2026.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, MGS benchmark yields (conventional, Jun-2031)

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Bank Negara Malaysia, MGS benchmark yields (conventional, Oct-2036)

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Malaysia, income determination
tax_bank_interest.note: PwC (last reviewed 16 Jun 2026): interest received by individuals on money deposited in approved institutions (licensed banks and financial institutions) is tax-exempt.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Malaysia, income determination
tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No savings certificate exists; interest from certain bonds and securities (including government securities) is exempt.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM), Deposit Insurance System
deposit_insurance_limit.note: RM250,000 per depositor per member bank; Islamic and conventional deposits are protected separately.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: BNM sets a maximum credit card finance charge in its credit card policy document, but we could not reach the document or a page stating the current figure.

equity_return_low.note: The KLCI has made little price progress over the past decade, so the low case is a dividend-like 3%.

equity_return_base.sourceName: 5-year MGS 3.68% plus a modest premium; weak KLCI 10-year record
equity_return_base.note: Base set about 3.7 points above the tax-free safe rate (about 2.8%), below the 4-point limit, because the KLCI's 10-year record is weak.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Long-run Malaysian and regional equity returns
equity_return_high.note: High case with a full equity premium over government bonds.

gold_return_low.sourceName: US-dollar gold trend; ringgit exchange rate (BNM)
gold_return_low.note: Gold can stall for a decade, and the ringgit has strengthened in 2026.

gold_return_base.sourceName: US-dollar gold trend; ringgit exchange rate (BNM midrate 4.06 per USD)
gold_return_base.note: Long-run dollar gold trend of about 5% plus about 0.5% a year of ringgit depreciation.

gold_return_high.sourceName: US-dollar gold trend; ringgit exchange rate (BNM)
gold_return_high.note: High case for a strong gold cycle.

fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case just below the 12-month average fixed deposit rate. Safe MYR rates: commercial-bank average fixed deposit 3-month 2.15%, 12-month 2.19% (BNM, Sep 2026); 3-month treasury bill 2.98%, 5-year MGS 3.68%, 10-year MGS 3.89% (BNM, 30 Oct 2026); OPR 2.75%; interest on bank deposits is tax-exempt for individuals.

fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case between the 12-month fixed deposit average and the 3-month treasury bill yield, reachable through deposit promotions and money market funds. Safe MYR rates: commercial-bank average fixed deposit 3-month 2.15%, 12-month 2.19% (BNM, Sep 2026); 3-month treasury bill 2.98%, 5-year MGS 3.68%, 10-year MGS 3.89% (BNM, 30 Oct 2026); OPR 2.75%; interest on bank deposits is tax-exempt for individuals.

fixed_income_return_high.note: High case at the 5-year government bond yield. Safe MYR rates: commercial-bank average fixed deposit 3-month 2.15%, 12-month 2.19% (BNM, Sep 2026); 3-month treasury bill 2.98%, 5-year MGS 3.68%, 10-year MGS 3.89% (BNM, 30 Oct 2026); OPR 2.75%; interest on bank deposits is tax-exempt for individuals.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: No industry-wide life claim settlement ratio published by Bank Negara Malaysia or the life insurance association was found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life is widely sold, but we could not read published premium rates or a credible premium guide in ringgit.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay found.

health_premium_table.note: No published medical insurance premium rates by age found.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure, SH.XPD.OOPC.CH.ZS)
oop_health_share.note: Latest World Bank (WHO GHED) value is for 2023, older than 2025.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Headline CPI (DOSM via Trading Economics); private medical cost trend
goal_inflation_health.note: The health CPI covers subsidised public care, but private hospital and insurance costs have risen much faster, so we plan about 3.5 points above general inflation.

goal_inflation_education.note: Public schooling is largely free while private and tertiary fees rise faster, so we plan 1 point above general inflation.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN)

life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years derived from expected age at death by current age; secondary source for UN WPP.

support_ratio.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant (via populationpyramid.net)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 11.4 in 2025, 17.6 in 2040 and 38.7 in 2065 (populationpyramid.net year pages).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Wikipedia, Retirement age (Malaysia row); secondary source
retirement_age_default.note: Retirement age 60 for private employees (raised from 55 in 2013); EPF savings can be fully withdrawn from 55. Secondary source because official Act and labour ministry pages could not be read.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Wikipedia, Retirement age (Malaysia note on civil servants); secondary source
retirement_age_government.note: Civil servants retire at 60; the public-sector union has asked for 62 but the government has no immediate plan to raise it. Official public service department site failed TLS verification.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case just below the 12-month average fixed deposit rate. Safe MYR rates: commercial-bank average fixed deposit 3-month 2.15%, 12-month 2.19% (BNM, Sep 2026); 3-month treasury bill 2.98%, 5-year MGS 3.68%, 10-year MGS 3.89% (BNM, 30 Oct 2026); OPR 2.75%; interest on bank deposits is tax-exempt for individuals.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: BNM OPR 2.75%, average 12-month fixed deposit 2.19%, 3-month treasury bill 2.98%
retirement_return_base.note: Base case at about the policy rate, below the tax-free treasury bill yield and above the average 1-year deposit rate. Safe MYR rates: commercial-bank average fixed deposit 3-month 2.15%, 12-month 2.19% (BNM, Sep 2026); 3-month treasury bill 2.98%, 5-year MGS 3.68%, 10-year MGS 3.89% (BNM, 30 Oct 2026); OPR 2.75%; interest on bank deposits is tax-exempt for individuals.

retirement_return_high.note: High case at the 5-year government bond yield. Safe MYR rates: commercial-bank average fixed deposit 3-month 2.15%, 12-month 2.19% (BNM, Sep 2026); 3-month treasury bill 2.98%, 5-year MGS 3.68%, 10-year MGS 3.89% (BNM, 30 Oct 2026); OPR 2.75%; interest on bank deposits is tax-exempt for individuals.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: EPF dividend record (5.35%-6.30% in 2021-2025, 6.15% for 2025; via Wikipedia); MGS yields
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix with weak equity.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: EPF dividend record (5.35%-6.30% in 2021-2025, 6.15% for 2025; via Wikipedia); MGS yields
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Half equity at 6.5% and half bonds near 3.5%, a little below EPF's recent dividends.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: EPF dividend record (5.35%-6.30% in 2021-2025, 6.15% for 2025; via Wikipedia); MGS yields
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case slightly above EPF's recent dividend rates.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Bantuan Warga Emas (Social Welfare Department) pays a monthly allowance to poor elderly people, but the JKM website was unreachable and we could not read the current amount.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Bantuan Warga Emas is means-tested and for older people (60+); could not read the official criteria page (JKM site unreachable).

gratuity_rule.note: The Employment Act 1955 gives termination and lay-off benefits only when employment is ended by the employer; there is no statutory end-of-service gratuity on retirement.

public_pension_scheme.note: EPF is a provident fund, not a pension: employees pay 11% and employers 12-13% of wages (rates as of 2012 per source); the retirement account can be withdrawn in full from 55. Dividends 6.15% for 2025, 6.30% for 2024; legal minimum 2.5%. inflationLinked false because benefits are a lump sum.

dps.note: No common monthly recurring deposit product.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No standing government savings certificate for individuals.

tbill_91d.note: Sold at auction to institutions; individuals reach them only through money market funds.

tbond_5y.note: Individuals can buy MGS through some banks' bond counters or bond funds.

equity_fund.note: Unit trusts and exchange-traded funds are widely sold to retail investors.

gold.note: Gold bars and coins are sold by jewellers and banks.

insuranceComplaints.name: Financial Markets Ombudsman Service (FMOS)
insuranceComplaints.note: Formed by consolidating the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS) and SIDREC; covers insurance and takaful disputes.

oldAgeAllowance.name: Social Welfare Department (JKM), Bantuan Warga Emas

publicHealthCover.name: Ministry of Health Malaysia (subsidised public hospitals and clinics)
